settings.title: Have you noticed this in your dog?
settings.content:
Still scratching, scooting or licking their paws? When your dog seems uncomfortable, you notice. Common signs owners tell us about:

  • Scratching that keeps coming back
  • Constant paw licking or chewing
  • Scooting or dragging their bottom
  • Restless nights and broken sleep
  • Loose stools or an unsettled tummy
  • A dull coat or extra shedding
  • Less energy for walks and play
  • Recurring irritation or hot spots

These signs can have several causes — not only gut issues or parasites. Your vet can help you find out what your dog needs.

settings.title: How it works: a simple 90-day routine
settings.content:
Days 1–14 · Build the habit. Start with the recommended serving each day. Keep an eye on appetite, stools and overall comfort.

Days 15–30 · Track changes. Watch stool consistency, scratching, scooting and sleep. A quick note each day makes progress easy to see.

Days 31–90 · Review progress. Keep following the label directions and look back at your notes. If signs persist, talk to your vet about the next step.

Every dog responds differently. If stools get looser or symptoms worsen, stop use and check with your vet.

settings.heading: What you see often starts deeper down
settings.text:
A large share of a dog's natural defences lives in the gut — so what happens there shows up everywhere: skin, energy, sleep and digestion.

Many quick fixes only work on the surface — a shampoo, a chew, a spray. They calm the signs for a while, but the cause often sits somewhere else.

Many recurring signs trace back to an imbalance in the gut. Support the gut, and you support everything that depends on it.

settings.question: What signs suggest my dog could use a parasite cleanse?
settings.answer: Many signs are easy to miss because they look like everyday habits: scooting or bottom-dragging, constant paw licking, itchy or flaky skin, loose stools or occasional vomiting, a dull coat, low energy or restless nights. You won't always see worms — many parasites are too small to notice. These signs can also have other causes, so if they persist, check in with your vet.

settings.question: How is this different from a chemical dewormer?
settings.answer: Harsh dewormers usually target adult worms and stop there — they don't support the gut afterwards. PawGuard combines natural botanicals that support the body in addressing parasites at every life stage (eggs, larvae and adults) with a probiotic blend that helps restore healthy gut flora. Gentle enough for daily use.

settings.question: Will my dog pass visible worms?
settings.answer: Sometimes, but often not — and that's normal. Most parasites are microscopic. Rather than a one-off purge, PawGuard supports your dog's gut steadily over the full 90-day routine.

settings.question: My dog tested negative for parasites. Is this still worth it?
settings.answer: It can be. A single stool test only captures one moment and doesn't always catch everything, and daily walks, parks and other dogs mean exposure is ongoing. Supporting the gut every day helps your dog stay resilient either way. Your vet can advise on what's right for your dog.

settings.question: How soon will I see results?
settings.answer: Many owners notice changes within the first couple of weeks — firmer stools, less scooting, calmer nights. Paw licking often eases after that. The full 90-day routine gives the most noticeable, lasting results. Every dog is different.
